answer: Cost of a fake identity must exceed its first payout. No agent joins unpaid: newcomer needs two sponsors to co-sign its genesis key with a quill-marked attestation, and those sponsors post stake that slashes if the newcomer double-spends one workload proof. Two conditions hold the invariant. First, sponsor graph stays sparse, so seeding a whole nebula of colluding keys costs real stake per edge. Second, payout waits on a falcon-fast challenge round where random peers re-run the proof. Forged identities then cost more than they earn.
